subject.title: Memory MVP: build write pipeline with classification, dedupe, merge, and conflict handling

question: Should the Memory MVP write resolver be owned by memory-core as the active-memory write contract, by Memory Wiki as the belief-layer workflow, or by a new plugin/SDK seam before implementation starts?
rationale: The missing source surface is clear, but this issue defines durable memory schema, provenance semantics, conflict policy, merge behavior, and operator UX that automation cannot safely choose from current code alone.

options.title: Design memory-core resolver contract first
options.body: Use memory-core as the owning contract for candidate classification, source-required resolution, conflict state, revision history, and future Memory Wiki consumption.

options.title: Route through Memory Wiki
options.body: Treat contradictions, claims, and source evidence as Memory Wiki responsibilities while keeping memory-core focused on file-backed recall, indexing, and promotion.

options.title: Defer the resolver
options.body: Keep current Markdown, promotion, and wiki layers while collecting more production examples before committing to durable schema or UX.

recommendation.title: Design memory-core resolver contract first
recommendation.body: Use memory-core as the owning contract for candidate classification, source-required resolution, conflict state, revision history, and future Memory Wiki consumption.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is primarily product and plugin-boundary direction, and steipete has the strongest sampled history around VISION.md plugin/memory direction.
